title: Jerusalem and Al-Aqsa
subtitle: Why Al-Aqsa matters in Islam and how to discuss Jerusalem with justice
summary: Jerusalem and Al-Aqsa hold a unique place in Islamic faith and history. The Quran connects the Prophet's night journey to the Farthest Mosque, and Muslims honor Jerusalem as a land of prophets and worship. Islam also requires justice and respect for every community connected to the city.

sections.title: Why Jerusalem and Al-Aqsa Matter in Islam
sections.body: Jerusalem is sacred to more than one religious community. For Muslims, Al-Aqsa is connected to the Prophet's night journey, the earlier prophets, and the first direction of prayer. Recognizing Jewish and Christian attachments does not weaken the Islamic claim; it reflects the Quranic command to speak truthfully and act justly.

sections.title: What Muslims Mean by Al-Aqsa
sections.body: In common Muslim usage, Al-Aqsa can refer to the mosque and, more broadly, to the blessed sanctuary compound in Jerusalem. Its religious importance is grounded in the Quran and the Prophet's teachings, while details about buildings, access, and governance belong to history and law. Quran 22:40 names monasteries, churches, synagogues, and mosques when explaining the protection of places where Allah is worshipped. Muslims do not treat Al-Aqsa as sacred because of a modern political slogan; they honor it as part of the prophetic inheritance.

sections.title: The Isra and Mi'raj in Islamic Sources
sections.body: The Quran says that Allah took His servant by night from the Sacred Mosque to the Farthest Mosque, whose surroundings He blessed (Quran 17:1). Muslim hadith and tafsir identify the Farthest Mosque with the sanctuary in Jerusalem and connect the journey with the Prophet's ascent, the Mi'raj. This is a foundational reason Muslims love Al-Aqsa. It establishes religious significance; questions of modern sovereignty and archaeology must be discussed with historical evidence and without denying the dignity of the people who live there.

sections.title: How to Study a Shared Sacred City
sections.body: Study Jerusalem through more than one kind of source: Quran and hadith for Islamic belief, archaeology and documentary history for the past, and reliable reporting for the present. Do not confuse a religious conviction with a claim that requires historical evidence. The city deserves precision, and no political argument justifies hatred of Jews, Christians, Muslims, or any civilian population.

sections.title: Key Takeaways: Jerusalem and Al-Aqsa
sections.body: Al-Aqsa matters to Muslims because Allah blessed its surroundings and connected it to the Prophet's night journey and the history of revelation. That devotion should produce worship, truthfulness, protection of sacred places, and justice for people—not hatred or careless claims. Muslims can uphold Al-Aqsa's Islamic significance while acknowledging the city's layered history and treating every innocent person with dignity.

quranVerses.arabic: بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ سُبْحَٰنَ ٱلَّذِىٓ أَسْرَىٰ بِعَبْدِهِۦ لَيْلًۭا مِّنَ ٱلْمَسْجِدِ ٱلْحَرَامِ إِلَى ٱلْمَسْجِدِ ٱلْأَقْصَا ٱلَّذِى بَٰرَكْنَا حَوْلَهُۥ لِنُرِيَهُۥ مِنْ ءَايَٰتِنَآ ۚ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلسَّمِيعُ ٱلْبَصِيرُ
quranVerses.translation: Exalted is He who took His Servant by night from al-Masjid al-Haram to al-Masjid al-Aqsa, whose surroundings We have blessed, to show him of Our signs. Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Seeing.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: ٱلَّذِينَ أُخْرِجُوا۟ مِن دِيَٰرِهِم بِغَيْرِ حَقٍّ إِلَّآ أَن يَقُولُوا۟ رَبُّنَا ٱللَّهُ ۗ وَلَوْلَا دَفْعُ ٱللَّهِ ٱلنَّاسَ بَعْضَهُم بِبَعْضٍۢ لَّهُدِّمَتْ صَوَٰمِعُ وَبِيَعٌۭ وَصَلَوَٰتٌۭ وَمَسَٰجِدُ يُذْكَرُ فِيهَا ٱسْمُ ٱللَّهِ كَثِيرًۭا ۗ وَلَيَنصُرَنَّ ٱللَّهُ مَن يَنصُرُهُۥٓ ۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَقَوِىٌّ عَزِيزٌ
quranVerses.translation: [They are] those who have been evicted from their homes without right - only because they say, "Our Lord is Allah." And were it not that Allah checks the people, some by means of others, there would have been demolished monasteries, churches, synagogues, and mosques in which the name of Allah is much mentioned. And Allah will surely support those who support Him. Indeed, Allah is Powerful and Exalted in Might.
